Perturbation methods build approximate analytical solutions to differential equations by expanding the solution in powers of a small parameter. Multiple-scale (two-timing) expansions treat slow and fast variables as independent, separating a slowly varying average from fast oscillations, and are suited to stiff or periodically forced systems with well separated time scales.

## Multiple scales for periodically forced catalytic kinetics (2025)

Colombo Tedesco and co-workers applied a two-time-scale expansion to the coverage equations of dynamic catalysis, with the small parameter defined as the smallest rate-constant amplitude times the forcing period. The leading order gives cycle-averaged coverages from linear algebraic equations (neglecting the covariance between rate constants and coverages), and the first-order correction gives the limit cycle by direct integration with a zero-mean condition. The covariance itself serves as a diagnostic: it grows as the time-scale separation or small-amplitude assumptions fail ([Colombo Tedesco et al. 2025](/papers/colombotedesco2025/)). Summary: [colombotedesco2025](/papers/colombotedesco2025/).
